comparability_caveats: These sequences are now adaptation targets. No claim of unseen-chain generalization is supported by this study. The previous study and its frozen-test exclusion rules remain unchanged.
The paper trained on each named sequence and retained the best reward across training and periodic epsilon-zero evaluations. Its best contacts are not guaranteed final-policy performance.
The paper reports best long-sequence training runs (length >= 36) were performed only once and parameters were manually chosen.
The 60mer best of 49 contacts arose during training; the paper reports periodic evaluated models did not attain it.
For the 50mer, Table 1 reports energy -34 but Table 3 reports HCSA -31, Attn-DRL -29 and EHA -28. Neither 34 nor 31 contacts is independently certified optimal here.

The paper uses five relative directions, coordinate bounds, symmetry constraints and DFS validity checks. Our local lattice controls use legal unoccupied absolute axial placements, a fixed initial +x bond, no bounding box and no DFS completion test.
Paper episode budgets do not establish equal sample or compute cost versus native queries, physical placement attempts, feedback updates or search.
Local controls are legal-action references, not Adapt-1 selectors. They are not exact matched controls for an unmasked native policy.
scoring: Contacts are unordered nonconsecutive H-H residue pairs at Manhattan distance one; energy is minus contacts.
